description: AMENDMENT 0001 The purpose of Amendment 0001 to Solicitation W519TC-26-Q-JOC1 is to extend the closing date to 16 November 2026, 5:00PM CST. All other terms and conditions of the solicitation remain unchanged. ****************************************************************************************************************************************************** The Solicitation will be for projects within the McAlester Army Ammunition Plant (MCAAP). The contractor shall perform all work required as specified within the Statement of Work (SOW) in each individual Task Order (TO). The general description of the work of this Job Order Contract (JOC) includes, but is not limited to, a broad range of sustainability, repair, and maintenance (SRM), and minor construction work on real property at MCAAP. The work is required in support of Directorate of Public Works (DPW) activities. The contract comprises a one-year (1) base period with four one-year (1) option periods. This requirement is a total small business set-aside under NAICS 236220 � Commercial and Institutional Building Construction, size standard $45M. Individual task orders will be firm-fixed price and contain the following limitations: The Base Year will have an established value with a minimum limit of $5,000 and a maximum limit of $19,800,000. Option Periods 1 through 4 will have an established value with a minimum of $5,000 and a maximum limit of $19,800,000. The total maximum value of all Task Orders issued under this Master Agreement (including all option years) shall not exceed $99,000,000.00. EVALUATION OF PROPOSALS Proposal shall contain the complete solicitation number (W519TC-26-Q-JOC1), and a complete detailed proposal for the sample TO as specified in the EXAMPLE Statement of Work (SOW) titled, "50�x100�x18� Red Iron Storage Facility". The sample TO is for evaluation purposes ONLY. The single, comprehensive coefficient proposed for the sample TO, representing all direct and indirect costs not included in the RSMeans Unit Price Book (UPB), shall be the coefficient utilized by the contractor for all future TOs. This single coefficient is the only price factor to be proposed. Any questions should be addressed no later than 30 OCT 2026 (10 days before end of solicitation) and sent via email to Jessica Parr at jessica.m.parr2.civ@army.mil. Sample proposal is DUE 09 NOV 2026 no later than 5:00PM CST via email to jessica.m.parr2.civ@army.mil. Work under any TO issued as the result of any contract awarded shall be performed in strict accordance with the TO SOW, the broad SOW incorporated in this solicitation, and all applicable federal, state and local environment laws, regulations, and policies No work shall commence without a formally executed Task Order. The process shall be as follows: A. Joint Scope Meeting: Upon identifying a need, MCAAP and Contractor shall conduct a site visit to jointly define the precise Scope of Work (SOW). B. Proposal Submission: The Contractor shall submit a detailed price proposal based strictly on the agreed SOW, utilizing the Unit Price Book (UPB) line items, exact quantities, and the applicable Adjustment Factor. C. Issuance: Upon MCAAP review and approval of the proposal, MCAAP will issue a signed Task Order detailing the exact firm-fixed price and the Required Completion Date. If a required task or material is not listed in the UPB, it shall be classified as a Non-Pre-Priced (NPP) item. For any Non-Pre-Priced (NPP) item required during the performance of a Task Order, the Contractor must obtain and submit a minimum of three (3) independent quotes from subcontractors or suppliers. The Contractor may then apply their accepted NPP Markup Factor to the lowest responsive quote. NPP items must not exceed 10% of the total cost of any individual Task Order. Payment & Performance Bonds: The Contractor shall provide a Payment and Performance Bond for 100% of the value of any individual Task Order exceeding $35,000 (or as dictated by local statute). Insurance: The Contractor must maintain Commercial General Liability, Worker�s Compensation, and Automobile insurance for the duration of this Master Agreement, naming the Owner as an additional insured. The price offer shall be comprised of coefficients. A coefficient, as defined in AFARS 5117.9001, is "a numerical factor that represents costs (generally indirect costs) not considered to be included in RSM unit prices (e.g., general and administrative and other overhead costs, insurance costs, bonding and alternative payment protection costs, protective clothing, equipment rental, and also contractor's profit)." c. Coefficients proposed and accepted upon award are multiplied by unit prices in RSM to price a job or project on individual task orders. The coefficients proposed are incorporated in the Job Order Contract (JOC). Offerors who submit separate coefficients for separate line items in RSM will be considered unacceptable and the offer will be rejected. Coefficients are limited to three decimal places and submitted as a whole number. For example: 1.015. d. When developing proposals, use "Average" rows in RSM if shown. If only "Minimum/Maximum� rows are shown, use the "Minimum" row. Also, use the column entitled "Total Bare Costs" which includes material, labor, and equipment. Do not use the column "Total Incl O & P." e. The offeror's price coefficient must include but is not limited to the following: 1. Overhead 2. Profit (prime and subcontractors) 3. Insurance 4. description: THERE IS NO SOLICITATION AVAILABLE AT THIS TIME. The solicitation for this effort is expected to be available on or before 16 November 2026. THIS SYNOPSIS IS A PRE-SOLICITATION NOTIFICATION OF THE GOVERNMENTS INTENT TO AWARD A SOLE SOURCE CONTRACT TO THE BOEING COMPANY, IAW MP 5332.7 Funds Availability "Notice to Offeror(s)/Suppliers(s): Funds are not presently available for this effort. No award will be made until funds are available. The Government reserves the right to not solicit this requirement or cancel the solicitation after issuance, either before or after the closing date. in the event the Government cancels the solicitation, the Government has no obligation to reimburse an offeror for any costs" This acquisition is for a supply. This is a production contract for the Conventional Air Launched Cruise Missile (CALCM) / Air Launched Cruise Missile (ALCM) Test Instumentation Kit (CATIK); managed by the Air Force Nuclear Weapons Center Missile Sustainment Division (AFNWC/NDM) at Tinker AFB Oklahoma. The CATIK is a universal kit used in ALCM test flights that processes multiple subsystem inputs-including flight computer, engine, navigation, range safety, warhead, and instrumentation signals utilizing a Common Core Unit (CCU) PCM MUX output routed to an embedded encryption device to provide secure PCM telemetry data. The scope of this effort encompasses the procurement, assembly, testing, qualification, and delivery of CATIK shipsets, Line Replaceable Units (LRUs), Shop Replaceable Units (SRUs), and FlightTermination System (FTS) components, utilizing Government Furnished Property (GFP) tracked within CAV-AF. CONTRACT TYPE, PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE AND SMALL BUSINESS SUBCONTRACTING The current acquisition strategy is to issue a definitive Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contract for a base production lot if 15 each CATIKs, with contract options to purchase 15 each Flight Termination Batteries and 15 each Instrumentation Batteries. The Contract Line Item Number (CLIN) structure used for recurring production and engineering will be Firm Fixed Price. Delivery is expected to complete within 18 months after award. The Government has determined that this effort will not be a small business set aside. The contractor will be required to meet all small business particitpation requirements included in the contract and fulfill all the requirements of the subcontracting plan included in the contract.

title: (EAR048) Repair Fire Alarm System Eareckson Air Station Facilities
description: **30 OCT 2026 Update** See the attached file �EAR048_Industry Questions and GOV Response, 30 OCT 2026� for U.S. Government (USG) responses to industry questions. Please continue to submit questions to the Point of Contact (POC) listed below. The USG will post responses on a weekly basis. **End of 30 OCT 2026 Update ** REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) / MARKET INTELLIGENCE NOTICE Notice: This is a Request for Information (RFI) for market intelligence and for informational purposes only. This announcement does not constitute a Solicitation or a Request for Proposal (RFP), and no solicitation is currently available. Participation in this RFI is strictly voluntary. The Government will not be obligated to award any agreement or contract because of this RFI, nor will it reimburse respondents for any costs associated with the preparation or submission of information. Submitting a response will not affect a firm�s ability to submit a proposal should a formal solicitation be issued in the future. NAICS Code: 236220 � Commercial and Institutional Building Construction (Note: While Other Transaction Authority is not subject to FAR-based small business regulations, this NAICS code is provided for market research to help the Government understand the size and demographics of the interested industrial base.) Small Business Size Standard: $45 Million PROJECT OVERVIEW The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Alaska District, has a requirement for the site-wide repair and replacement of fire alarm systems at Eareckson Air Station (Shemya Island, Alaska). The project will replace aging and non-compliant fire alarm systems across multiple facilities to meet current UFC 3-600-01, NFPA 72, and life-safety requirements. Existing systems are outdated or non-functional, creating risk to personnel and mission on this remote installation. The Government is now pursuing a wireless (or hybrid wireless) fire alarm architecture that significantly reduces or eliminates the need for extensive buried fiber optic infrastructure, thereby addressing the primary cost driver while achieving full code compliance. Key project components include: � Demolition of existing fire alarm control panels, initiating devices, notification appliances, conduit, and wiring across affected buildings � Installation of a new wireless/hybrid addressable fire alarm system, including wireless devices, gateways/repeaters for campus-wide RF coverage, limited residual hard-wired elements only where essential, and integration with supervisory/monitoring capabilities � RF coverage analysis, specialty detection in hazardous (Class I) locations associated with fuel systems, cybersecurity compliance, multi-shift training, testing, commissioning, and phased turnover � Phased execution by building or geographic area to accommodate remote-island logistics and minimize operational impact Estimated Acquisition Magnitude: Between $27M and $33M Planned Acquisition Strategy: Anticipated to utilize Progressive Design Build via Other Transaction Authority (OTA) The Alaska District is conducting market intelligence to assess industry capability and interest in supporting this effort utilizing an Other Transaction (OT) Agreement under the authority of 10 U.S.C. � 2808a, Facility Construction or Repair: Transactions Other Than Contracts and Grants. This authority is distinct from the Department of Defense prototype OT authorities commonly associated with 10 U.S.C. � 4021 and 4022. This authority is intended for military construction and repair projects that involve testing and experimentation associated with new and emergent construction technologies to achieve potential benefits such as enhanced mission resilience, improved installation support, or cost and schedule reduction. The anticipated delivery method is Progressive Design-Build. Design and Pre-Construction Services - The OT Awardee shall assist the Government collaboratively in advancing the wireless/hybrid fire alarm design, performing RF coverage analysis and site investigations, supporting the UFC waiver process, validating and refining project requirements, and developing progressively more detailed open-book cost and schedule information. Design is expected to advance from approximately 0�15% at award to an agreed interim milestone (target approximately 65%) sufficient for reliable Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP) development. Final Design and Construction - Upon reaching an agreed-upon level of design, the Awardee will propose a Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP) or Firm-Fixed-Price for final design and construction. If the price is accepted and required funding/approvals (including UFC waiver status) are in place, the Government will authorize Phase 2 execution via modification. Construction is expected to be authorized in staggered packages by building or geographic area to allow early turnover of priority facilities. If a fair and reasonable price cannot be agreed upon, or if other conditions prevent proceeding, the Government retains an �off-ramp� to complete the project via alternative methods while retaining rights to the design developed during Phase 1.
